$comment: EVENTS: domain events from every source (live, replay-<run>, parity), the durable, deduplicated feed logbook reads (ADR 0001, point 1; paddock#36). One stream for every source: pruning a replay is a delete by src in logbook (paddock#45), not a stream of its own.
subjects: twr.v1.*.evt.> covers every event subject in contracts' subjects.yaml, twr.v1.<src>.evt.<sid>.<area>.<what>.
max_age 30 d (2592000000000000 ns): ADR 0001's starting value, so a consumer that is down for weeks can still catch up. Lauda measures whether 30 d is right.

max_bytes 1 GiB (1073741824): an event is a few hundred bytes (session.ended with its summary a few KB), so a session of 50 laps is tens of KB, and 30 d of driving and replays stays far below 1 GiB. The limit is a backstop so the stream cannot fill the disk (paddock#36, decision of 2026-10-24).
discard old: if the backstop is ever reached, the oldest events go first, never new ones.
duplicate_window 2 min (120000000000 ns): events carry a deterministic Nats-Msg-Id (ADR 0002, point 4), so a replay or a restarted ecu that republishes within 2 min stores each event once.
max_msg_size -1: bounded by the server's max_payload (1 MiB by default). max_msgs, max_msgs_per_subject and max_consumers -1: max_bytes and max_age are the limits.
num_replicas 1: one NATS server (ADR 0004). File storage so a server restart keeps the events.
name: EVENTS
description: Domain events from every source, kept 30 d, deduplicated on Nats-Msg-Id (paddock#36).
